title: Glass Slippers
subtitle: Beautiful, resplendent, and impossible to ignore. It might not fit perfectly, but we don't have any other choice.

items.text: The door is closed.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hi, it's Vertin.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Desert Flannel, is Ezra still with you?
After a while, the door is still closed.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Desert Flannel?
Silence is the only answer.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Spathodea has decided to supervise the construction herself, and Ulu is now with her at the site. I'm wondering how you are doing with Ezra.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No response. Are they ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Not in the room, I knew it.
A note has been left on the desk beside the bed.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "Showing Ezra what the world is like. Be right back."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "Desert Flannel."

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Watch your feet and your head.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: The people here never look down. That's how you get muddy shoes when you're out of here.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Here, take my hand.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Ms. Desert Flannel, what is this place? What are we doing here?

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Something that needs to be done, and something that needs to be said.
The deeper they go, the louder the cheering they hear from the crowd.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Hey! Big bloke, don't get in my way!
The big guy steps aside. A ray of light penetrates the air and pierces Ezra's eyes, and the only thing he can see is boundless white.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Emm ... this is ...

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: The warm-up of the rugby game. It's not a formal game, but the audience enthusiasm is burning. I mean ... it's hard to get the ticket.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: But I'm Desert Flannel, and I know people on the streets. Even when we're outside Melbourne.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Sorry, I've never watched any games, and I don't know the rules of rugby.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I ... I don't think I will understand any of this. Do you mind?

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: No, I'm cool with that, because the game is not what we are after.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: You see that guy over there? That's Tom, a shining new star in the NRL, the best fullback they've ever had. He's from the Melbourne Sail Car Club.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: They have a seagull as their club's mascot, with a fish and a chip in its mouth.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Yes ...? Okay ...?

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: And that bloke over there. That's Kip-Karl of the Hobart Blue Lake. He's the kind of player who knows how to really tackle. They call him the Unbreakable K.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: And lastly, I want you to look at that smaller guy. That's Russel. Doesn't look tough, does he? But he is the Slippery Jerboa, because, man, he is fast when he gets the ball.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: But what is this to do with us? I still don't understand ...

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Ezra.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Guess how many of them are arcanists?

items.speaker: Commentator
items.text: Nice one! Nice one! Russel made it again! Excellent interception!

items.speaker: Commentator
items.text: The key score! Now the Jerboa is as slippery as butter! Run, run for it, Russel! Victory is going to the Shepherds of Melbourne!
On the green field, Russel is roaring excitedly after his goal. He draws a cross symbolizing victory on his uniform stained with dirt and grass.

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: Russel! Russel! Russel! Russel!
Wave after wave, the cheer of the audience swells through the field.
Ezra, however, is pulled by a sudden force at his arm and heads out of the Stadium.
Inside a dark and long tunnel, Desert Flannel marches without hesitation.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Mankind is known for their physical resilience and endurance, that is to say ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Tom and Kip-Karl are humans, while Russel, whose skills and unpredictability are his strength, is an arcanist.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Hmm. A reasonable deduction!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Physical resilience and varied skills are indeed the respective features of mankind and arcanists.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: However, things are not as simple as they appear.
She stops at a door, turns the doorknob, and pushes it open.
Changing Room
What welcomes them is a mixed smell of sweat, dust, grass, and medicine, together with occasional curses.
Players, black and blue, are busy coming and going. Nobody has time to take care of these two trespassers.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: In fact, all of them are arcanists.

items.speaker: Russel
items.text: ... S**t, gimme that thing. *exhales*

items.speaker: Team Manager
items.text: Here ... Be careful, don't overdose. Painkillers are addictive, you know.

items.speaker: Team Manager
items.text: And the newspaper is gonna interview you champions, so don't get high in front of the camera. Hey, listen ...

items.speaker: Russel
items.text: Emm ...

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Sporting is great fun, but it can also be dangerous, especially for sports like rugby, MMA, or boxing, which involve a lot of intense physical contact.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: And the arcanists, who are good at healing, will naturally become the best athletes of all.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: … 15 minutes, that's all they take. Most of the arcane treatments take only 15 minutes to heal the patient. And before that happens, the athletes would just take painkillers to help themselves get through the game.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: And after that 15 minutes, they are refreshed and healthy, like those athlete dolls you'd find in the souvenir store.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: They can slide, impact like a maniac, and don't have to worry about missing any important sporting sessions if injured.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: This is an advantage?

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: That's right, an unbelievable advantage. But ... are they really as good as they look?

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Their glory comes with a price. Ligament damage and the irreversible tears keep recurring ...

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: But there is still an elephant in the room. It paces around, making noises which are unfit for the place, like this conversation we're having in the locker room.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: But on the sports field, where the blood boils, power and strength are the only things that matter. Nobody has the time to stop and ask what we are doing here, just like they don't have the time to notice the elephant.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Ten years ago, Margret of Broken Hill was invincible on the court.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: In August last year, she died on the last day of winter.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Did she die of recurrent injuries? It's very likely that arcanist athletes who repeatedly get injured and heal themselves would get hurt on the same body part in the future. Their body will become fragile. They might even twist their ankle from walking. Sometimes even break a bone or two.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: No. She died from an overdose.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: She needed a horrific amount of painkillers to ease her pain, so much that her body was overwhelmed.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: This, this is cruel!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: We have to report this to the Foundation and solve it once and for all. The athletes could have played in a safer way if given help.
It's rare to see the boy being so unsure and nervous. An astonished look takes over his pretty girlish face.
Desert Flannel ponders and looks at him.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: But what if I tell you the arcanists also don't have a choice?

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: For humans who have the talent for sports, they can win the medals with their physical strengths.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: So, arcanists have to make the most of their advantages to keep abreast with their competitors?
She silently nods.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I, I had no idea.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: I'm sorry, truly.
Desert Flannel once again puts her hand on his shoulder and pulls the boy into her arms in a sisterly embrace.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: I didn't mean to make you feel guilty, nor did I deliberately put you in pain. But Ezra, I was once one of them. I used to live on the prize money.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: I'm only telling the truth. It is happening every day, every moment, and every second. Drug addiction, premature senility, and irreversible physical damage ... This is almost a destined end for every arcanist athlete.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: And nobody is held accountable for this, not the clubs, or the hosts of the games. Drug abuse is a personal behavior, that's it.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Those people who are passionate about sports and don't wanna lead a life without them ... I have no idea how they would make a living or handle a quiet life, so I know they don't have much of a choice.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: The sport industry of humans is generous. They offer equal chances to human and arcanist athletes. But it's also cruel, and the athletes are like the girls in Cinderella story who wish their feet would fit the glass slippers.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: They have no choice but to cut off part of their heels to earn the glory.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: This ... this isn't fair. These sports and rules are not appropriate for arcanists. They, they have been treated unjustly. They aren't taken seriously and respected as athletes ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Is ... is Spathodea ... one of them ...?

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: That's why she was ... so furious ...
So the rumor that they are turning against each other is true!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Camera, this way. This is the human representative of the event ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: ...! You, you are that paparaz- ...?

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: This is not how a polite kid would address others, Mr. Ezra.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: I'm just a concerned journalist who run into you while reporting a rugby game.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Watch your mouth, mister! This is harassment!
She covers Ezra and rapidly moves backward, but behind them are still clicking cameras.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: We are cornered ...!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Then we will break his camera and let him know the price of being a long-tongued liar!
